column1: # The FALCO_CTF_REGISTRY grammar's shared case table (app#510, #507 review-5x R1#1).
# FALCO_CTF_REGISTRY is the `<registry>/<repository prefix>` that deploy-user.sh
# `*.image.repository`). The grammar is an OCI `host[:port]/path`: the host is DNS
# labels of [a-z0-9-] (lower case), an optional `:<1 to 5 digits>`, then path
# components that follow the OCI distribution grammar (alphanumerics joined by `.`,
# `_`, `__` or hyphens). A tag, a digest, a scheme and any `,` `=` are not in it.
# The LAST path component must be `falco-ctf`: the scoreboard ingest
# `falco-ctf-challenge`, and `${REGISTRY}/challenge` can only contain the first, so a
# registry that does not end in `falco-ctf` would deploy a workspace whose detections
# are silently never scored. (Stricter than the ingest's substring on purpose: a
# registry ending in `my-falco-ctf` would pass the ingest and is a reject here.)
# The grammar says a registry is SHAPED right, not that it exists or that the port is
# <= 65535 (the kubelet is the judge of that). There is no length bound: an
# over-long reference fails at the container runtime, it is not an injection.
# The grammar has NO Go definition: the shell literal is the definition. The readers:
#   - Go:    internal/catalog (deploy_operator_inputs_test.go) pins the header to the
#            shell literal, runs every row, and holds the `falco-ctf/challenge`
#            substring to the one in ingest.go.
#   - shell: charts/ctf-user/deploy-user.sh, run row by row as the env
# An empty value has no row: an empty FALCO_CTF_REGISTRY means "not set" (the chart
# default is kept), as it always has.
# The account id in the second baseline row is the all-zero placeholder, not a real one.
# Every shape-reject row ends in `/falco-ctf` (or is the `falco-ctf` part itself), so it
# is the SHAPE that rejects it, and the self-test can tell the two checks apart.
# Format: the same as internal/identity/testdata/seat-cases.tsv (see its header):
# {U+00EF}, line 1 the canonical `# pattern: ` literal. The table stays ASCII.
# The input is the value as the operator gives it, with the one exception that an
# empty value has no row (see below). A row is never dropped to make an
# implementation pass: the implementation that disagrees is the bug.
# --- baseline: the shapes a stand-up uses (synthetic values: the table is public)
# --- shape (every accept row ends in /falco-ctf: see the next block)
# --- the last component must be falco-ctf: the scoreboard ingest drops an event whose image repository does not contain falco-ctf/challenge, and ${REGISTRY}/challenge only contains it then
# --- a registry host: labels of [a-z0-9-], the first and the last a letter or digit
# --- a port: digits only, at most 5, one
# --- a path component: alphanumerics joined by `.`, `_`, `__` or hyphens (the OCI distribution grammar)
# --- what belongs to another value or to no value: a tag, a digest, a scheme, a query
# --- helm --set syntax: a `,` starts another key, `=` another assignment
# --- line breaks, a bidi control, a non-ASCII letter
